# Anatomical ROI comparison: mushroom body vs full FlyWire

**Status:** the subgraph extraction command and its synthetic fixture validation are implemented. Actual mushroom-body benchmark data must be generated by a verified run before a conclusion is drawn.

## Rationale

The existing whole-brain associative-retrieval experiment encodes every text feature by a deterministic hash into an arbitrary FlyWire root ID. It discards a biologically relevant dimension available in the original connectivity release: the **neuropil** where each presynaptic-postsynaptic connection was observed.

The release's `proofread_connections_783.feather` groups synaptic contacts by neuron pair AND anatomical neuropil, exposing the `neuropil` string and `syn_count` columns. The previous whole-brain converter aggregated across neuropils and therefore could not select a circuit based on anatomy. See https://zenodo.org/records/10676866 and its release description.

We can now obtain a more meaningful *region-restricted* adjacency without another downloader or a handmade network. The mushroom-body anatomical neuropils are a plausible first target for memory-oriented computation, but we do not assert that the cropped network alone captures the full fly's associative memory system.

## Exact conversion

With the unchanged, checksum-verified v783 original files acquired using `scripts/download_flywire_v783.py`, run:

```sh
python scripts/convert_flywire_feather.py \
  data/flywire_v783/proofread_connections_783.feather \
  data/flywire_v783/proofread_root_ids_783.npy \
  data/derived/flywire_v783_mb_csr.npz \
  --neuropil-prefix MB_ --prune-to-region
```

The converter checks root-ID membership against the full proofread list before pruning. It selects only rows whose release neuropil string starts with `MB_`, aggregates exact presynaptic/postsynaptic duplicate pairs across the selected regions, preserves positive synapse-count sums as evidence, and retains only neuron IDs incident to those selected contacts. The original full converter, with no optional flags, remains unchanged in behavior.

`MB_` is a regional label family, not a verified cell-class selector or neurotransmitter sign. The subgraph excludes contacts from the same neurons outside selected neuropils and may omit long-range inputs and outputs vital to the biological circuit. This is a *neuropil-local connectivity assay*, not a reconstructed complete mushroom-body model. Source data and scripts should be pinned by checksums/commits in the executed result.

## Matched experiment

Run a post-hoc diagnostic with the frozen 450-memory corpus, identical source split and encoder, seeds `31,37,43`, and compare: narrative-only TF-IDF, original MB topology graph-only and hybrid, and target-stub-rewired MB topology graph-only and hybrid.

```sh
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python scripts/run_associative_memory.py \
  --topology data/derived/flywire_v783_mb_csr.npz \
  --benchmark --seeds 31,37,43 \
  --output results/associative/flywire-v783-mb-three-seed.json
```

Report positive top-1, correct-and-accepted recall, contradiction false acceptance, absent-event false acceptance, and per-case disagreement with matched lexical and rewired controls. Also record node/edge counts, contact counts, sparse-computation cost and actual ROI labels represented.

## Interpretation and stop/go criteria

A within-MB improvement over its own rewired control would support the hypothesis that some biological connectivity structure is useful under this particular encoding. It would not alone demonstrate biologically plausible learning, persona memory, or superiority to all conventional memory systems.

Comparing MB against full FlyWire is confounded by node count, edge count and feature collision rates. A persuasive later experiment needs size- and budget-matched controls, independently reviewed novel probes, and perhaps mappings aligned with mushroom-body cell classes. Do not select positive examples after looking at the previous Pilot 04 challenge.

If the MB-based graph also matches or underperforms its rewired control, stop adding topology variations blindly. Prefer evidence-aware conventional memory retrieval until a specific anatomical encoding and plasticity hypothesis can be tested.


## Follow-on neuron-class encoder, distinct from ROI filtering

The official FlyWire annotation repository also contains a separate neuron-level table with \`root_id\`, \`cell_class\`, \`cell_sub_class\`, \`cell_type\`, \`top_nt\`, \`top_nt_conf\` and \`side\`. We should use this only after examining the ROI results: https://github.com/flyconnectome/flywire_annotations/blob/main/supplemental_files/Supplemental_file1_neuron_annotations.tsv .

That table changes independently of the original v783 publication, so pin an exact tagged annotation version and content checksum before mixing its neuron classes with the original connectivity. For reproducibility, the annotation blob observed at planning time was \`02e72f6c8161d3465f77fec0edf96c5d98027a9e\` on the annotations repository's main branch, which is not a fixed publication tag.

A subsequent, independently assessed experiment could restrict or steer cue encoding into labeled Kenyon-cell or mushroom-body input populations and constrain plasticity by documented cell class. Merely assigning text features randomly to neurons in an MB-labeled ROI remains anatomical borrowing rather than biologically faithful learning.


## Actual executed ROI outcome (2026-10-08)

The verified mushroom-body extraction and three-seed benchmark **have completed successfully**. The original description at the top of this document is a historical prospective protocol; the actual report supersedes its pending status. See [measured MB results](../results/associative/FLYWIRE_V783_MB_THREE_SEED_RESULTS.md) and [raw case-level JSON committed to Git](../results/associative/runs/flywire-mb-three-seed-run37836674947.json). Exact conversion metadata are [also committed](../results/associative/runs/flywire-mb-conversion-run37836674947.json). The biological MB topology did not improve correct-and-accepted recall over the rewired control under current hash encoding. Do not rerun solely to seek a more flattering post-hoc result.
